problem:
A particle $P$ of mass $4\,\text{kg}$ is subject to the external forces 

$$
{F}_{1}=⟨2,\,4{sin}^{3}⁡t⟩,\,{F}_{2}=⟨8\operatorname{sin}⁡2t-2,\,4\operatorname{sin}⁡t{cos}^{2}⁡t⟩,
$$

where ${F}_{1}$ and ${F}_{2}$ are measured in Newtons and $t>0$ is the time, in seconds. Given that the velocity of $P$ equals $⟨0,\,-1⟩\,\text{m/s}$ when $t=0\,\text{s},$ calculate the velocity vector of $P$ at $t=\frac{\pi }{2}\,\text{s}.$
worked_solution:
Newton's second law states that

$$
F=ma,
$$

 
where $F$ is the *resultant* force, $m$ is the mass, and $a$ is the acceleration.

The resultant force $F$ acting on $P$ equals the sum of the forces acting on $P.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F & ={F}_{1}+{F}_{2} \\  & =⟨2,\,4{sin}^{3}⁡t⟩+⟨8\operatorname{sin}⁡2t-2,\,4\operatorname{sin}⁡t{cos}^{2}⁡t⟩ \\  & =⟨2+8\operatorname{sin}⁡2t-2,\,4{sin}^{3}⁡t+4\operatorname{sin}⁡t{cos}^{2}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨8\operatorname{sin}⁡2t,\,4\operatorname{sin}⁡t({sin}^{2}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨8\operatorname{sin}⁡2t,\,4\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

By Newton's second law, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{F}{m} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot ⟨8\operatorname{sin}⁡2t,\,4\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩ \\  & =⟨2\operatorname{sin}⁡2t,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

To compute the velocity vector $v,$ we need to integrate the acceleration vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\int a\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int ⟨2\operatorname{sin}⁡2t,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩\,\text{d}t \\  & =⟨\int 2\operatorname{sin}⁡2t\,\text{d}t,\,\int \operatorname{sin}⁡t\,\text{d}t⟩ \\  & =⟨-\operatorname{cos}⁡2t,\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩+C\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is a (vector) constant of integration. 

We can solve for $C$ by substituting $v=⟨0,\,-1⟩\,\text{m/s}$ and $t=0\,\text{s}$ into the above, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨0,\,-1⟩ & =⟨-\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\cdot 0),\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡0⟩+C \\ ⟨0,\,-1⟩ & =⟨-1,\,-1⟩+C \\ C & =⟨1,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the velocity of $P$ at time $t$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =⟨-\operatorname{cos}⁡2t,\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩+⟨1,\,0⟩ \\  & =⟨1-\operatorname{cos}⁡2t,\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally  the velocity at $t=\frac{\pi }{2}$ equals

$$
\begin{aligned}v(\frac{\pi }{2}) & =⟨1-\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\cdot \frac{\pi }{2}),\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨2,\,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$
